messages.content: "請您進行一個統計t檢定，以檢查兩個獨立數據集的平均值是否有統計上的差異？第一個數據集，數據集A，包含以下整數：12、15、18、20、22、25、28、30、32、35。第二個數據集，數據集B，包含以下整數：14、17、19、21、23、26、29、31、33、36。請分別以顯著性水平0.05和0.01進行兩次檢定。"

function.name: t_test
function.description: Perform a statistical t-test to check if the means of two independent datasets are statistically different. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

alpha.description: Significance level for the test. Default is 0.05. This is a float type value.

message.reasoning:
The user wants us to perform a statistical t-test on two independent data sets and provide results at alpha=0.05 and alpha=0.01.

We have tool "functions.t_test". We need to call it with dataset_A list [12,...], dataset_B list [14,...]. The default alpha is 0.05 but we can specify both tests separately or run twice? They want separate significance levels; so likely do one test at alpha=0.05 then another at alpha=0.01. But maybe they expect output summarizing p-value etc. We'll use the tool once per alpha.

But note: The tool signature expects only one alpha param. So we'll call twice: first with alpha=0.05, second with alpha=0.01.

We'll produce JSON result from each call. Then interpret.

Let's compute manually quickly:

Dataset A: values: 12,15,18,20,22,25,28,30,32,35 (10 numbers)
Mean A: sum = let's calculate: 12+15=27, +18=45, +20=65, +22=87, +25=112, +28=140, +30=170, +32=202, +35=237. Mean = 237/10 = 23.7.

Variance A: Compute deviations squared:
(12-23.7)=-11.7^2=136.89
(15-23.7)= -8.7^2=75.69
(18-23.7)= -5.7^2=32.49
(20-23.7)= -3.7^2=13.69
(22-23.7)= -1.7^2=2.89
(25-23.7)=1.3^2=1.69
(28-23.7)=4.3^2=18.49
(30-23.7)=6.3^2=39.69
(32-23.7)=8.3^2=68.89
(35-23.7)=11.3^2=127.69
Sum squares = let's add: 136.89+75.69=212.58, +32.49=245.07, +13.69=258.76, +2.89=261.65, +1.69=263.34, +18.49=281.83, +39.69=321.52, +68.89=390.41, +127.69=518.10 approx. Sample variance s² = sum/(n-1)=518.10/9 ≈57.5667. Standard deviation sqrt ~7.590.

Dataset B: values: 14,17,19,21,23,26,29,31,33,36
Sum: 14+17=31,+19=50,+21=71,+23=94,+26=120,+29=149,+31=180,+33=213,+36=249. Wait double-check: Actually after adding 33 it's 213, plus 36 gives 249. Yes mean = 24.9.

Compute deviations squared:
14-24.9=-10.9^2=118.81
17-24.9=-7.9^2=62.41
19-24.9=-5.9^2=34.81
21-24.9=-3.9^2=15.21
23-24.9=-1.9^2=3.61
26-24.9=1.1^2=1.21
29-24.9=4.1^2=16.81
31-24.9=6.1^2=37.21
33-24.9=8.1^2=65.61
36-24.9=11.1^2=123.21
Sum squares: 118.81+62.41=181.22, +34.81=216.03, +15.21=231.24, +3.61=234.85, +1.21=236.06, +16.81=252.87, +37.21=290.08, +65.61=355.69, +123.21=478.90. Sample variance = 478.90 /9 =53.211... SD≈7.295.

Now conduct independent samples t-test assuming equal variances? Usually Welch's t-test uses unequal var assumption. Let's approximate using pooled variance? Might not matter much difference.

Pooled variance sp² = ((n1-1)s1²+(n2-1)s2²)/(n1+n2-2). n1=n2=10. So numerator = 9*57.567 + 9*53.211 = 517.103 + 479.899 =997.002. Denominator 18 -> sp²=55.389. Sp=√55.389=7.44.

Standard error SE = sp * √(1/n1 + 1/n2) = 7.44 * √(0.1+0.1)=7.44*√0.2=7.44*0.4472=3.327.

Difference in means d = 23.7-24.9 = -1.2.

T-statistic = d / SE = (-1.2)/3.327 = -0.3607.

Degrees freedom df = n1+n2-2 = 18.

Two-tailed p-value: For |t|=0.361, df=18, p > .70 probably. Use approximation: t critical for α=.05 two-sided df=18 is about ±2.101. Since our t magnitude < 2.101, fail to reject null. P-value around 0.72.

Thus at alpha=0.05 no significant difference. At alpha=0.01 also fails.

Alternatively could use Welch's t-test: se_welch = sqrt(s1²/n1 + s2²/n2) = sqrt(57.567/10 + 53.211/10) = sqrt(5.7567+5.3211)=sqrt(11.0778)=3.328 same as above basically because sample sizes equal. Degrees of freedom via Welch-Satterthwaite formula: df = (s1²/n1+s2²/n2)^2 / [(s1⁴/(n1²*(n1-1))) + (s2⁴/(n2²*(n2-1)))].

Calculate: s1²/n1 = 57.567/10=5.7567; s2²/n2=53.211/10=5.3211; Sum=11.0778; Square=122.78.

Denominator terms: s1⁴ = (57.567)^2 =3317.5 ; divide by (100*(9))? Wait n1²(n1-1)=100*9=900. So term1=3317.5/900=3.684. Similarly s2⁴=(53.211)^2=2831.5; denominator part2=2831.5/(100*9)=3.147. Sum denom=6.831. DF=122.78/6.831=17.98 ~18. Same as before.

So similar.

Hence p-value remains high.

Therefore answer: No evidence of difference at either significance level.

Also mention assumptions: independence, normality approximated due to small sample size but okay.
